title: Crema catalana
summary: A stovetop custard infused with lemon zest and cinnamon, chilled in shallow dishes and burnt on top to a thin crackling crust.

ingredients.note: pared in strips if you can

steps: Heat the almond milk, cream, lemon zest and cinnamon until steaming. Cover and leave 15 minutes to infuse, then strain.
Whisk the yolks, erythritol, xanthan gum and salt in a saucepan until smooth. Gradually whisk in the warm milk.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until the custard thickens and coats the spatula, about 80 °C (176 °F). Do not let it boil.
Pour into six shallow dishes, cool, then refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Just before serving, sprinkle each evenly with allulose and burn the top with a torch until amber.
dairy_free_notes: Coconut cream sets a little firmer and adds a coconut note that sits alongside the lemon and cinnamon.
tips: Unlike crème brûlée, this custard is cooked on the stove, not baked, and is traditionally flavoured with lemon and cinnamon instead of vanilla.

origin.history: Crema catalana is a stirred custard of Catalonia, flavoured with lemon and cinnamon and caramelised with a hot iron. Catalans claim it as one of Europe's oldest custard desserts and a forerunner of crème brûlée, though its exact age is debated. It is traditionally eaten on St Joseph's Day, 19 March, and is also called crema de Sant Josep.
